Sharded Services分片服务

— PDF 第 87 页 —

In Chapter 6, we saw the value of replicating stateless services for reliability, redundancy, and scaling. This chapter considers sharded services. With the replicated services that we introduced in Chapter 6, each replica was entirely homogeneous and capable of serving every request. In contrast to replicated services, with sharded services, each replica, or shard, is only capable of serving a subset of all requests. A load-balancing node, or root, is responsible for examining each request and distributing each request to the appropriate shard or shards for processing. The contrast between replicated and sharded services is represented in Figure 7-1.

在第 6 章中，我们看到了复制无状态服务在可靠性、冗余与扩展方面的价值。本章讨论分片服务。在第 6 章介绍的复制服务中，每个副本完全同质，能够处理每一个请求。与复制服务不同，在分片服务中，每个副本（或称分片）只能处理全部请求的一个子集。一个负载均衡节点（或称根节点）负责检查每个请求，并将其分发到合适的一个或多个分片进行处理。复制服务与分片服务之间的对比如图 7-1 所示。

Replicated services are generally used for building stateless services, whereas sharded services are generally used for building stateful services. The primary reason for sharding the data is because the size of the state is too large to be served by a single machine. Sharding enables you to scale a service in response to the size of the state that needs to be served.

复制服务通常用于构建无状态服务，而分片服务通常用于构建有状态服务。对数据进行分片的主要原因，是状态太大，单机无法承载。分片让你能够根据需要服务的状态规模来扩展服务。

Sharding is not exclusively for stateful services, though. Sometimes sharding can also be useful for stateless services for the purpose of isolation. Failures in distributed systems can sometimes come from the input requests to the system (“poison requests”) in a replicated system—if the poison requests come in a large enough volume, they can take down all of the replicas. In such systems, sharding can form an isolation boundary that protects the majority of the requests from the poison ones. Though the poison requests may take out the entire shard, that will only be a fraction of the requests that the system processes.

不过，分片并非只适用于有状态服务。有时，为了隔离目的，分片对无状态服务也很有用。在分布式系统中，故障有时来自系统收到的输入请求（即“毒丸请求”）——在复制系统中，如果毒丸请求的量足够大，它们可以把所有副本全部拖垮。在这类系统中，分片可以形成一道隔离边界，保护大多数请求免受毒丸请求的影响。虽然毒丸请求可能让整个分片宕掉，但那也只占系统所处理请求的一小部分。

— PDF 第 88 页 —

Sharded Caching分片缓存

To completely illustrate the design of a sharded system, this section provides a deep dive into the design of a sharded caching system. A sharded cache is a cache that sits between the user requests and the actual frontend implementation. A high-level diagram of the system is shown in Figure 7-2.

为了完整说明分片系统的设计，本节深入剖析一个分片缓存系统的设计。分片缓存是位于用户请求与实际前端实现之间的一层缓存。该系统的高层示意图如图 7-2 所示。

In Chapter 4, we discussed how an ambassador could be used to distribute data to a sharded service. This section discusses how to build that service. When designing a sharded cache, there are a number of design aspects to consider:

在第 4 章中，我们讨论了如何使用 ambassador（ ambassador 容器）将数据分发到分片服务。本节讨论如何构建该服务。在设计分片缓存时，有若干设计方面需要考虑：

  • Why you might need a sharded cache为什么你可能需要分片缓存
  • The role of the cache in your architecture缓存在你的架构中扮演的角色
  • Replicated sharded caches复制的分片缓存
  • The sharding function分片函数

Why You Might Need a Sharded Cache为什么你可能需要分片缓存

Reminder: the primary reason for sharding any service is to increase the size of the data being stored in the service. To understand how this helps a caching system, imagine the following system: each cache has 10 GB of RAM available to store results, and can serve 100 requests per second (RPS). Suppose then that our service has a total of 200 GB possible results that could be returned, and an expected 1,000 RPS.

提醒：对任何服务进行分片的主要原因，都是为了增大该服务所能存储的数据规模。要理解这对缓存系统有何帮助，请设想如下系统：每个缓存有 10 GB 内存可用于存储结果，每秒可服务 100 个请求（RPS）。再假设我们的服务共有 200 GB 可能被返回的结果，预期 RPS 为 1,000。

— PDF 第 89 页 —

Clearly, we need 10 replicas of the cache in order to satisfy 1,000 RPS (10 replicas × 100 requests per second per replica). The simplest way to deploy this service would be as a replicated service, as described in Chapter 6. But deployed this way, the distributed cache can only hold a maximum of 5% (10 GB/200 GB) of the total data set that we are serving. This is because each cache replica is independent, and thus each cache replica stores roughly the exact same data in the cache. This is great for redundancy, but pretty terrible for maximizing memory utilization. If instead, we deploy a 10-way sharded cache, we can still serve the appropriate number of RPS (10 × 100 is still 1,000), but because each cache serves a completely unique set of data, we are able to store 50% (10 × 10 GB/200 GB) of the total data set. This tenfold increase in cache storage means that the memory for the cache is much better utilized, since each key exists only in a single cache. The more data we store in the cache, the faster the overall system will be able to operate since more requests can be served from the cache.

显然，我们需要 10 个缓存副本才能满足 1,000 RPS（10 副本 × 每副本每秒 100 请求）。部署该服务最简单的方式，就是像第 6 章描述的那样作为复制服务部署。但这样部署时，分布式缓存最多只能装下我们所服务数据集的 5%（10 GB / 200 GB）。这是因为每个缓存副本相互独立，因此每个缓存副本在缓存中存的大致是完全相同的数据。这对冗余来说很好，但对最大化内存利用率来说却相当糟糕。反过来，如果我们部署一个 10 路分片缓存，仍然可以服务相应数量的 RPS（10 × 100 仍是 1,000），但由于每个缓存服务的是完全唯一的数据集，我们就能存下总数据集的 50%（10 × 10 GB / 200 GB）。缓存存储量提升十倍，意味着缓存内存得到更好利用，因为每个键只存在于单个缓存中。我们在缓存中存的数据越多，整个系统运行得就越快，因为更多请求可以直接由缓存服务。

The Role of the Cache in System Performance缓存在系统性能中的角色

In Chapter 6 we discussed how caches can be used to optimize end-user performance and latency, but one thing that wasn’t covered was the criticality of the cache to your application’s performance, reliability, and stability.

在第 6 章中，我们讨论了如何使用缓存来优化终端用户的性能与延迟，但没有涉及一点：缓存对你应用的性能、可靠性与稳定性到底有多关键。

Put simply, the important question for you to consider is: if the cache were to fail, what would the impact be for your users and your service?

简而言之，你需要思考的重要问题是：如果缓存挂了，对你的用户和服务会有什么影响？

When we discussed the replicated cache, this question was less relevant because the cache itself was horizontally scalable, and failures of specific replicas would only lead to transient failures. Likewise, the cache could be horizontally scaled in response to increased load without impacting the end user.

在讨论复制缓存时，这个问题没那么要紧，因为缓存本身是水平可扩展的，个别副本的故障只会导致短暂失败。同样，缓存可以针对负载增加进行水平扩展，而不影响终端用户。

This changes when you consider sharded caches. Because a specific user or request is always mapped to the same shard, if that shard fails, that user or request will always miss the cache until the shard is restored. Given the nature of a cache as transient data, this miss is not inherently a problem, and your system must know how to recalculate the data. However, this recalculation is inherently slower than using the cache directly, and thus it has performance implications for your end users.

当你考虑分片缓存时，情况就变了。因为某个特定用户或请求总是映射到同一个分片，如果该分片故障，那么在分片恢复之前，该用户或请求将始终缓存未命中。鉴于缓存本质上是瞬态数据，这种未命中本身不是问题，你的系统必须知道如何重新计算数据。然而，这种重新计算本质上比直接使用缓存慢，因此会对终端用户的性能产生影响。

The performance of your cache is defined in terms of its hit rate. The hit rate is the percentage of the time that your cache contains the data for a user request. Ultimately, the hit rate determines the overall capacity of your distributed system and affects the overall capacity and performance of your system.

缓存的性能以命中率来衡量。命中率是指缓存中恰好含有某用户请求所需数据的时间百分比。归根结底，命中率决定了分布式系统的整体容量，并影响系统的整体容量与性能。

Imagine, if you will, that you have a request-serving layer that can handle 1,000 RPS. After 1,000 RPS, the system starts to return HTTP 500 errors to users. If you place a cache with a 50% hit rate in front of this request-serving layer, adding this cache increases your maximum RPS from 1,000 RPS to 2,000 RPS. To understand why this is true, you can see that of the 2,000 inbound requests, 1,000 (50%) can be serviced by the cache, leaving 1,000 requests to be serviced by your serving layer. In this instance, the cache is fairly critical to your service, because if the cache fails, then the serving layer will be overloaded and half of all your user requests will fail. Given this, it likely makes sense to rate your service at a maximum of 1,500 RPS rather than the full 2,000 RPS. If you do this, then you can sustain a failure of half of your cache replicas and still keep your service stable.

请设想：你有一个请求服务层，能处理 1,000 RPS。超过 1,000 RPS 后，系统就开始向用户返回 HTTP 500 错误。如果你在这个请求服务层前面放一个命中率 50% 的缓存，加入这个缓存会把最大 RPS 从 1,000 提升到 2,000。要理解为什么，你可以看到：在 2,000 个入站请求中，有 1,000 个（50%）可由缓存服务，剩下 1,000 个请求由服务层处理。在这种情况下，缓存对你的服务相当关键，因为如果缓存故障，服务层就会过载，你一半的用户请求都会失败。鉴于此，把服务额定为最大 1,500 RPS 而不是满额 2,000 RPS 可能更合理。这样做之后，即便一半缓存副本故障，你仍能维持服务稳定。

— PDF 第 90 页 —

But the performance of your system isn’t just defined in terms of the number of requests that it can process. Your system’s end-user performance is defined in terms of the latency of requests as well. A result from a cache is generally significantly faster than calculating that result from scratch. Consequently, a cache can improve the speed of requests as well as the total number of requests processed. To see why this is true, imagine that your system can serve a request from a user in 100 milliseconds. You add a cache with a 25% hit rate that can return a result in 10 milliseconds. Thus, the average latency for a request in your system is now 77.5 milliseconds. Unlike maximum requests per second, the cache simply makes your requests faster, so there is somewhat less need to worry about the fact that requests will slow down if the cache fails or is being upgraded. However, in some cases, the performance impact can cause too many user requests to pile up in request queues and ultimately time out. It’s always recommended that you load test your system both with and without caches to understand the impact of the cache on the overall performance of your system.

但系统性能并不仅仅由它能处理的请求数来定义。系统的终端用户性能还由请求延迟来定义。缓存返回的结果通常比从头计算要快得多。因此，缓存不仅能提升请求处理总数，还能加快请求速度。要理解为什么，请设想：你的系统处理一个用户请求需要 100 毫秒。你加了一个命中率 25%、能在 10 毫秒内返回结果的缓存。于是系统中请求的平均延迟现在变成了 77.5 毫秒。与最大每秒请求数不同，缓存只是让你的请求变快，因此对“缓存故障或升级时请求会变慢”这件事，担忧可以少一些。但在某些情况下，性能影响会导致过多用户请求在请求队列中堆积，最终超时。始终建议你在有缓存和无缓存两种情况下都对系统做负载测试，以了解缓存对系统整体性能的影响。

Finally, it isn’t just failures that you need to think about. If you need to upgrade or redeploy a sharded cache, you cannot just deploy a new replica and assume it will immediately take the existing load. A newly created cache shard doesn’t have any data stored in memory. Responses are cached as they are received in response to user requests. A newly deployed cache needs to be “warmed up” or filled with responses before it can provide maximal benefit. Deploying a new version of a sharded cache will generally result in temporarily losing some capacity. Another, more advanced option is to replicate your shards.

最后，你需要考虑的不只是故障。如果你需要升级或重新部署分片缓存，不能只是部署一个新副本就指望它立刻承接现有负载。新创建的缓存分片内存中没有任何数据。响应是在响应用户请求的过程中被逐步缓存下来的。新部署的缓存需要“预热”——被响应数据填满——之后才能发挥最大效用。部署分片缓存的新版本，通常会暂时损失一部分容量。另一个更高级的选项是对分片进行复制。

Replicated Sharded Caches复制的分片缓存

Sometimes your system is so dependent on a cache for latency or load that it is not acceptable to lose an entire cache shard if there is a failure or you are doing a rollout. Alternatively, you may have so much load on a particular cache shard that you need to scale it to handle the load. For these reasons, you may choose to deploy a sharded replicated service. A sharded replicated service combines the replicated service pattern described in Chapter 6 with the sharded pattern described in previous sections. In a nutshell, rather than having a single server implement each shard in the cache, a replicated service is used to implement each cache shard.

有时，你的系统在延迟或负载上如此依赖缓存，以至于在故障或发布时损失一整个缓存分片是不可接受的。或者，某个缓存分片上的负载可能非常大，你需要扩展它来应对负载。由于这些原因，你可能选择部署一个分片复制服务。分片复制服务把第 6 章描述的复制服务模式与前面几节描述的分片模式结合起来。简而言之，缓存中的每个分片不再由单台服务器实现，而是用一个复制服务来实现每个缓存分片。

— PDF 第 91 页 —

This design is obviously more complicated to implement and deploy, but it has several advantages over a simple sharded service. Most importantly, by replacing a single server with a replicated service, each cache shard is resilient to failures and is always present during failures. Rather than designing your system to be tolerant to performance degradation resulting from cache shard failures, you can rely on the performance improvements that the cache provides. Assuming that you are willing to over-provision shard capacity, this means that it is safe for you to do a cache rollout during peak traffic, rather than waiting for a quiet period for your service.

这种设计在实现和部署上显然更复杂，但相比简单的分片服务有几个优势。最重要的是，用复制服务替换单台服务器后，每个缓存分片都能弹性应对故障，在故障期间始终可用。你不必把系统设计成对缓存分片故障所导致的性能下降保持容忍，而是可以依赖缓存所带来的性能提升。假设你愿意超额配置分片容量，这意味着你可以在流量高峰期间安全地进行缓存发布，而不必等到服务的静默时段。

Additionally, because each replicated cache shard is an independent replicated service, you can scale each cache shard in response to its load; this sort of “hot sharding” is discussed at the end of this chapter.

此外，由于每个复制的缓存分片都是一个独立的复制服务，你可以根据每个缓存分片自身的负载对其进行扩展；这种“热分片”将在本章末尾讨论。

Hands On: Deploying an Ambassador and Memcache for a Sharded Cache实战：为分片缓存部署 ambassador 与 Memcache

In Chapter 4 we saw how to deploy a sharded Redis service. Deploying a sharded memcache is similar.

在第 4 章中，我们看到了如何部署分片 Redis 服务。部署分片 memcache 与之类似。

First, we will deploy memcache as a Kubernetes StatefulSet:

首先，我们把 memcache 部署为一个 Kubernetes StatefulSet：

apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: StatefulSet
metadata:
  name: sharded-memcache
spec:
  serviceName: "memcache"
  replicas: 3
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: memcache
    spec:
      terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 10
      containers:
      - name: memcache
        image: memcached
        ports:
        - containerPort: 11211
          name: memcache

Save this to a file named memcached-shards.yaml, and you can deploy this with kubectl create -f memcached-shards.yaml. This will create three containers running memcached.

把它保存为 memcached-shards.yaml 文件，然后用 kubectl create -f memcached-shards.yaml 部署。这会创建三个运行 memcached 的容器。

— PDF 第 92 页 —

As with the sharded Redis example, we also need to create a Kubernetes Service that will create DNS names for the replicas we have created. The service looks like this:

与分片 Redis 示例一样，我们还需要创建一个 Kubernetes Service，为已创建的副本生成 DNS 名称。该 Service 如下：

apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: memcache
  labels:
    app: memcache
spec:
  ports:
  - port: 11211
    name: memcache
  clusterIP: None
  selector:
    app: memcache

Save this to a file named memcached-service.yaml and deploy it with kubectl create -f memcached-service.yaml. You should now have DNS entries for memcache-0.memcache, memcache-1.memcache, etc. As with Redis, we can use these names to configure twemproxy:

把它保存为 memcached-service.yaml 文件，并用 kubectl create -f memcached-service.yaml 部署。现在你应该有了 memcache-0.memcache、memcache-1.memcache 等 DNS 记录。与 Redis 一样，我们可以用这些名称来配置 twemproxy：

memcache:
  listen: 127.0.0.1:11211
  hash: fnv1a_64
  distribution: ketama
  auto_eject_hosts: true
  timeout: 400
  server_retry_timeout: 2000
  server_failure_limit: 1
  servers:
   - memcache-0.memcache:11211:1
   - memcache-1.memcache:11211:1
   - memcache-2.memcache:11211:1

In this config, you can see that we are serving the memcache protocol on localhost:11211 so that the application container can access the ambassador. We will deploy this into our ambassador pod using a Kubernetes ConfigMap object that we can create with: kubectl create configmap --from-file=nutcracker.yaml twem-config.

在这个配置中可以看到，我们在 localhost:11211 上提供 memcache 协议服务，以便应用容器能够访问 ambassador。我们将用一个 Kubernetes ConfigMap 对象把它部署到 ambassador pod 中，创建命令为：kubectl create configmap --from-file=nutcracker.yaml twem-config。

Finally, all of the preparations are done, and we can deploy our ambassador example. We define a pod that looks like this:

最后，所有准备工作就绪，我们可以部署 ambassador 示例了。我们定义如下 pod：

apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: sharded-memcache-ambassador
spec:
  containers:
    # This is where the application container would go, for example
    # - name: nginx
— PDF 第 93 页 —
    #   image: nginx
    # This is the ambassador container
    - name: twemproxy
      image: ganomede/twemproxy
      command:
      - nutcracker
      - -c
      - /etc/config/nutcracker.yaml
      - -v
      - 7
      - -s
      - 6222
      volumeMounts:
      - name: config-volume
        mountPath: /etc/config
  volumes:
    - name: config-volume
      configMap:
        name: twem-config

You can save this to a file named memcached-ambassador-pod.yaml, and then deploy it with:

你可以把它保存为 memcached-ambassador-pod.yaml 文件，然后用以下命令部署：

kubectl create -f memcached-ambassador-pod.yaml

Of course, we don’t have to use the ambassador pattern if we don’t want to. An alternative is to deploy a replicated shard router service. There are trade-offs between using an ambassador versus using a shard routing service. The value of the service is a reduction of complexity. You don’t have to deploy the ambassador with every pod that wants to access the sharded memcache service; it can be accessed via a named and load-balanced service. The downside of a shared service is twofold. First, because it is a shared service, you will have to scale it larger as demand load increases. Second, using the shared service introduces an extra network hop that will add some latency to requests and contribute network bandwidth to the overall distributed system.

当然，如果你不愿意，也不必使用 ambassador 模式。另一种做法是部署一个复制的分片路由服务。使用 ambassador 与使用分片路由服务之间存在权衡。共享 Service 的价值在于降低复杂度：你不必在每个想访问分片 memcache 服务的 pod 旁都部署 ambassador；它可以通过一个具名的、负载均衡的 Service 来访问。共享服务的缺点有两方面。第一，因为它是共享服务，随着需求负载增加，你必须把它扩展得更大。第二，使用共享服务会引入额外一跳网络，这会给请求增加一些延迟，并给整个分布式系统增加网络带宽开销。

To deploy a shared routing service, you need to change the twemproxy configuration slightly so that it listens on all interfaces, not just localhost:

要部署一个共享路由服务，你需要稍微修改 twemproxy 配置，让它监听所有网卡而不只是 localhost：

memcache:
  listen: 0.0.0.0:11211
  hash: fnv1a_64
  distribution: ketama
  auto_eject_hosts: true
  timeout: 400
  server_retry_timeout: 2000
  server_failure_limit: 1
  servers:
   - memcache-0.memcache:11211:1
   - memcache-1.memcache:11211:1
   - memcache-2.memcache:11211:1
— PDF 第 94 页 —

You can save this to a file named shared-nutcracker.yaml, and then create a corresponding ConfigMap using kubectl:

你可以把它保存为 shared-nutcracker.yaml 文件，然后用 kubectl 创建相应的 ConfigMap：

kubectl create configmap --from-file=shared-nutcracker.yaml shared-twem-config

Then you can turn up the replicated shard routing service as a Deployment:

然后你可以把这个复制的分片路由服务作为一个 Deployment 启动：

apiVersion: extensions/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: shared-twemproxy
spec:
  replicas: 3
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: shared-twemproxy
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: twemproxy
        image: ganomede/twemproxy
        command:
        - nutcracker
        - -c
        - /etc/config/shared-nutcracker.yaml
        - -v
        - 7
        - -s
        - 6222
        volumeMounts:
        - name: config-volume
          mountPath: /etc/config
      volumes:
      - name: config-volume
        configMap:
          name: shared-twem-config

If you save this to shared-twemproxy-deploy.yaml, you can create the replicated shard router using kubectl:

如果你把它保存为 shared-twemproxy-deploy.yaml，就可以用 kubectl 创建这个复制的分片路由：

kubectl create -f shared-twemproxy-deploy.yaml

To complete the shard router, we have to declare a load balancer to process requests:

要完成分片路由，我们还必须声明一个负载均衡器来处理请求：

kind: Service
apiVersion: v1
metadata:
  name: shard-router-service
spec:
  selector:
    app: shared-twemproxy
  ports:
    - protocol: TCP
— PDF 第 95 页 —
      port: 11211
      targetPort: 11211

This load balancer can be created using kubectl create -f shard-router-service.yaml.

这个负载均衡器可以用 kubectl create -f shard-router-service.yaml 创建。

An Examination of Sharding Functions剖析分片函数

So far we’ve discussed the design and deployment of both simple sharded and replicated sharded caches, but we haven’t spent very much time considering how traffic is routed to different shards. Consider a sharded service where you have 10 independent shards. Given some specific user request Req, how do you determine which shard S in the range from zero to nine should be used for the request? This mapping is the responsibility of the sharding function. A sharding function is very similar to a hashing function, which you may have encountered when learning about hashtable data structures. Indeed, a bucket-based hashtable could be considered an example of a sharded service. Given both Req and Shard, then the role of the sharding function is to relate them together, specifically:

到目前为止，我们讨论了简单分片缓存与复制分片缓存的设计和部署，但还没有花太多时间考虑流量是如何路由到不同分片的。设想一个分片服务，你有 10 个相互独立的分片。给定某个具体的用户请求 Req，你如何确定该用 0 到 9 之间的哪个分片 S 来处理该请求？这种映射就是分片函数的职责。分片函数与哈希函数非常相似——你在学习哈希表数据结构时可能遇到过哈希函数。事实上，基于桶的哈希表就可以被看作分片服务的一个例子。给定 Req 与 Shard，分片函数的作用就是把它们关联起来，具体来说：

Shard = ShardingFunction(Req)

Commonly, the sharding function is defined using a hashing function and the modulo (%) operator. Hashing functions are functions that transform an arbitrary object into an integer hash. The hash function has two important characteristics for our sharding:

通常，分片函数是用一个哈希函数和取模（%）运算符来定义的。哈希函数是把任意对象变换为一个整数哈希值的函数。对我们的分片而言，哈希函数有两个重要特性：

Determinism: The output should always be the same for a unique input.

确定性：对于同一个唯一输入，输出应当始终相同。

Uniformity: The distribution of outputs across the output space should be equal.

均匀性：输出在整个输出空间上的分布应当均匀。

For our sharded service, determinism and uniformity are the most important characteristics. Determinism is important because it ensures that a particular request R always goes to the same shard in the service. Uniformity is important because it ensures that load is evenly spread between the different shards.

对我们的分片服务而言，确定性和均匀性是最重要的两个特性。确定性之所以重要，是因为它保证某个特定请求 R 总是被送到服务中的同一个分片。均匀性之所以重要，是因为它保证负载在不同分片之间均匀分布。

Fortunately for us, modern programming languages include a wide variety of high-quality hash functions. However, the outputs of these hash functions are often significantly larger than the number of shards in a sharded service. Consequently, we use the modulo operator (%) to reduce a hash function to the appropriate range. Returning to our sharded service with 10 shards, we can see that we can define our sharding function as:

幸运的是，现代编程语言内置了多种多样的高质量哈希函数。然而，这些哈希函数的输出范围通常远大于分片服务中的分片数量。因此，我们用取模运算符（%）把哈希函数的值规约到合适的范围。回到那个有 10 个分片的分片服务，我们可以这样定义分片函数：

Shard = hash(Req) % 10
— PDF 第 96 页 —

If the output of the hash function has the appropriate properties in terms of determinism and uniformity, those properties will be preserved by the modulo operator.

如果哈希函数的输出在确定性和均匀性方面具备恰当的性质，那么这些性质会被取模运算符保留下来。

Selecting a Key选择键

Given this sharding function, it might be tempting to simply use the hashing function that is built into the programming language, hash the entire object, and call it a day. The result of this, however, will not be a very good sharding function.

有了这个分片函数后，你可能会图省事，直接用编程语言内置的哈希函数对整个对象做哈希就完事。然而，这样得到的分片函数并不好。

To understand this, consider a simple HTTP request that contains three things:

要理解这一点，请设想一个简单的 HTTP 请求，它包含三样东西：

  • The time of the request请求的时间
  • The source IP address from the client客户端的源 IP 地址
  • The HTTP request path (e.g., /some/page.html)HTTP 请求路径（例如 /some/page.html）

If we use a simple object-based hashing function, shard(request), then it is clear that {12:00, 1.2.3.4, /some/file.html} has a different shard value than {12:01, 5.6.7.8, /some/file.html}. The output of the sharding function is different because the client’s IP address and the time of the request are different between the two requests. But of course, in most cases, the IP address of the client and the time of the request don’t impact the response to the HTTP request. Consequently, instead of hashing the entire request object, a much better sharding function would be shard(request.path). When we use request.path as the shard key, then we map both requests to the same shard, and thus the response to one request can be served out of the cache to service the other.

如果我们用一个简单的基于对象的哈希函数 shard(request)，那么很显然 {12:00, 1.2.3.4, /some/file.html} 的分片值与 {12:01, 5.6.7.8, /some/file.html} 不同。分片函数输出不同，是因为这两个请求的客户端 IP 地址和请求时间不同。但当然，在大多数情况下，客户端 IP 地址和请求时间并不会影响 HTTP 请求的响应。因此，与其对整个请求对象做哈希，更好的分片函数是 shard(request.path)。当我们用 request.path 作为分片键时，这两个请求就被映射到同一个分片，于是其中一个请求的响应就可以从缓存中取出，用来服务另一个请求。

Of course, sometimes client IP is important to the response that is returned from the frontend. For example, client IP may be used to look up the geographic region that the user is located in, and different content (e.g., different languages) may be returned to different IP addresses. In such cases, the previous sharding function shard(request.path) will actually result in errors, since a cache request from a French IP address may be served a result page from the cache in English. In such cases, the cache function is too general, as it groups together requests that do not have identical responses.

当然，有时客户端 IP 对前端返回的响应是重要的。例如，客户端 IP 可能被用来查找用户所在的地理区域，不同 IP 地址可能返回不同内容（例如不同语言）。在这种情况下，前面那个分片函数 shard(request.path) 实际上会导致错误，因为来自法国 IP 地址的缓存请求可能被从缓存中返回一个英文结果页。在这种情况下，这个缓存函数过于笼统，因为它把响应并不相同的请求归到了一组。

Given this problem, it would be tempting then to define our sharding function as shard(request.ip, request.path), but this sharding function has problems as well. It will cause two different French IP addresses to map to different shards, thus resulting in inefficient sharding. This shard function is too specific, as it fails to group together requests that are identical. A better sharding function for this situation would be:

鉴于这个问题，你可能会想把分片函数定义为 shard(request.ip, request.path)，但这个分片函数同样有问题。它会让两个不同的法国 IP 地址映射到不同分片，从而导致分片效率低下。这个分片函数过于具体，因为它没能把完全相同的请求归并到一起。在这种情况下，更好的分片函数是：

shard(country(request.ip), request.path)
— PDF 第 97 页 —

This first determines the country from the IP address, and then uses that country as part of the key for the sharding function. Thus, multiple requests from France will be routed to one shard, while requests from the United States will be routed to a different shard.

它先从 IP 地址确定国家，然后把该国家作为分片函数键的一部分。于是，来自法国的多个请求会被路由到一个分片，而来自美国的请求会被路由到另一个分片。

Determining the appropriate key for your sharding function is vital to the optimal design of a sharded system. Determining the correct shard key requires an understanding of the requests that you expect to see.

为分片函数选择恰当的键，对分片系统的最优设计至关重要。确定正确的分片键，需要你对自己预期会遇到的请求有深入理解。

Consistent Hashing Functions一致性哈希函数

Setting up the initial shards for a new service is relatively straightforward: you set up the appropriate shards and the roots to perform the sharding, and you are off to the races. However, what happens when you need to change the number of shards in your sharded service? Such “re-sharding” is often a complicated process.

为一个新服务搭建初始分片相对直接：你搭好合适的分片和执行分片的根节点，就可以开工了。然而，当你需要改变分片服务中的分片数量时会发生什么？这种“再分片”往往是一个复杂的过程。

To understand why this is true, consider the sharded cache previously examined. Certainly, scaling the cache from 10 to 11 replicas is straightforward to do with a container orchestrator, but consider the effect of changing the scaling function from hash(Req) % 10 to hash(Req) % 11. When you deploy this new scaling function, a large number of requests are going to be mapped to a different shard than the one they were previously mapped to. In a sharded cache, this is going to temporarily cause a dramatic increase in your miss rate until the cache is repopulated with responses for the new requests that have been mapped to that cache shard by the new sharding function. In the worst case, rolling out a new sharding function for your sharded cache will be equivalent to a complete cache failure.

要理解为何如此，请回顾前面分析过的分片缓存。当然，用容器编排器把缓存从 10 个副本扩到 11 个很简单，但请考虑把分片函数从 hash(Req) % 10 改成 hash(Req) % 11 所带来的影响。当你部署这个新的分片函数时，大量请求会被映射到与之前不同的分片上。在分片缓存中，这会在一段时间内导致未命中率急剧上升，直到缓存重新填入那些被新分片函数映射到该缓存分片的新请求的响应。在最坏情况下，为分片缓存推出一个新的分片函数，等价于一次彻底的缓存故障。

To resolve these kinds of problems, many sharding functions use consistent hashing functions. Consistent hashing functions are special hash functions that are guaranteed to only remap # keys / # shards, when being resized to # shards. For example, if we use a consistent hashing function for our sharded cache, moving from 10 to 11 shards will only result in remapping < 10% (K / 11) keys. This is dramatically better than losing the entire sharded service.

为了解决这类问题，许多分片函数采用一致性哈希函数。一致性哈希函数是一类特殊的哈希函数，当分片数量调整为 # shards 时，它保证只有 # keys / # shards 数量的键会被重新映射。例如，如果我们对分片缓存使用一致性哈希函数，从 10 个分片扩到 11 个分片时，只会有不到 10%（K / 11）的键被重新映射。这远比丢掉整个分片服务要好得多。

Hands On: Building a Consistent HTTP Sharding Proxy实战：构建一个一致性 HTTP 分片代理

To shard HTTP requests, the first question to answer is what to use as the key for the sharding function. Though there are several options, a good general-purpose key is the request path as well as the fragment and query parameters (i.e., everything that makes the request unique). Note that this does not include cookies from the user or the language/location (e.g., EN_US). If your service provides extensive customization to users or their location, you will need to include them in the hash key as well.

要对 HTTP 请求做分片，首先要回答的问题是：用什么作为分片函数的键。虽然有若干选项，但一个不错的通用键是请求路径以及片段和查询参数（即使请求唯一的所有部分）。注意，这不包括用户的 cookie 或语言/地区（例如 EN_US）。如果你的服务针对用户或其所在地提供了大量定制，你也需要把它们纳入哈希键。

— PDF 第 98 页 —

We can use the versatile nginx HTTP server for our sharding proxy:

我们可以用功能丰富的 nginx HTTP 服务器来做分片代理：

worker_processes  5;
error_log  error.log;
pid        nginx.pid;
worker_rlimit_nofile 8192;

events {
  worker_connections  1024;
}

http {
    # define a named 'backend' that we can use in the proxy directive
    # below.
    upstream backend {
        # Has the full URI of the request and use a consistent hash
        hash $request_uri consistent
        server web-shard-1.web;
        server web-shard-2.web;
        server web-shard-3.web;
    }

    server {
        listen localhost:80;
        location / {
            proxy_pass http://backend;
        }
    }
}

Note that we chose to use the full request URI as the key for the hash and use the key word consistent to indicate that we want to use a consistent hashing function.

注意，我们选择用完整的请求 URI 作为哈希键，并使用关键字 consistent 来表明我们希望使用一致性哈希函数。

Sharded Replicated Serving分片复制服务

Most of the examples in this chapter so far have described sharding in terms of cache serving. But, of course, caches are not the only kinds of services that can benefit from sharding. Sharding is useful when considering any sort of service where there is more data than can fit on a single machine. In contrast to previous examples, the key and sharding function are not a part of the HTTP request, but rather some context for the user.

本章到目前为止的大多数例子，都是从缓存服务的角度来描述分片的。但当然，缓存并不是唯一能从分片受益的服务类型。只要某类服务的数据量超过单机容量，分片就有用武之地。与前面的例子不同，这里的键和分片函数并不来自 HTTP 请求本身，而是来自用户的某种上下文。

For example, consider implementing a large-scale multiplayer game. Such a game world is likely to be far too large to fit on a single machine. However, players who are distant from each other in this virtual world are unlikely to interact. Consequently, the world of the game can be sharded across many different machines. The sharding function is keyed off of the player’s location so that all players in a particular location land on the same set of servers.

例如，设想实现一个大规模多人在线游戏。这样的游戏世界很可能太大，无法放进单机。然而，在这个虚拟世界中相距遥远的玩家之间不太可能发生交互。因此，游戏世界可以分片到许多不同的机器上。分片函数以玩家位置为键，使得某个特定位置的所有玩家都落到同一组服务器上。

— PDF 第 99 页 —

Hot Sharding Systems热分片系统

Ideally the load on a sharded cache will be perfectly even, but in many cases this isn’t true, and “hot shards” appear because organic load patterns drive more traffic to one particular shard.

理想情况下，分片缓存上的负载会完全均匀，但在许多情况下并非如此；由于自然的负载模式把更多流量导向某个特定分片，就会出现“热分片”。

As an example of this, consider a sharded cache for a user’s photos; when a particular photo goes viral and suddenly receives a disproportionate amount of traffic, the cache shard containing that photo will become “hot.” When this happens, with a replicated sharded cache, you can scale the cache shard to respond to the increased load. Indeed, if you set up autoscaling for each cache shard, you can dynamically grow and shrink each replicated shard as the organic traffic to your service shifts around. An illustration of this process is shown in Figure 7-3. Initially the sharded service receives equal traffic to all three shards. Then the traffic shifts so that Shard A is receiving four times as much traffic as Shard B and Shard C. The hot sharding system moves Shard B to the same machine as Shard C, and replicates Shard A to a second machine. Traffic is now, once again, equally shared among replicas.

举个例子，设想一个用户照片的分片缓存；当某张照片突然病毒式传播、收到不成比例的流量时，包含该照片的缓存分片就会变“热”。出现这种情况时，对于复制的分片缓存，你可以扩展该缓存分片以应对增长的负载。事实上，如果你为每个缓存分片设置了自动扩缩容，就可以随着服务自然流量的转移，动态地伸缩每个复制分片。这个过程如图 7-3 所示。最初，分片服务向三个分片均匀接收流量。然后流量发生转移，使得分片 A 收到的流量是分片 B 和分片 C 的四倍。热分片系统把分片 B 移到与分片 C 同一台机器上，并把分片 A 复制到第二台机器上。流量现在再次在各副本之间均分。

— PDF 第 100 页 —

Summary小结

This chapter introduced the concept of sharding, which directs particular requests to particular groups of machines instead of load-balancing all traffic to all replicas of a service. An example was given of how sharding can significantly improve the efficiency and performance of a caching system attached to a serving API. Sharding is not just useful for caching, however. Systems like large-scale open world game servers and databases can scale beyond the size limits of a single machine by sharding their data across multiple different shard servers. Sharding also helps with isolation, limiting the blast radius of poison requests to a subset of all servers. Setting up a sharded system requires a careful understanding and design of both the shard key and the key hashing function. Identifying the right way to partition your data can often make the difference between a scalable system and one which runs into bottlenecks as it scales. Understanding the details of sharding is critical to building larger and more complex distributed systems.

本章介绍了分片的概念：它把特定请求导向特定的机器组，而不是把所有流量负载均衡到服务的所有副本上。文中举例说明了分片如何显著提升附着于服务 API 的缓存系统的效率与性能。不过，分片不仅对缓存有用。像大规模开放世界游戏服务器和数据库这样的系统，可以通过把数据分片到多个不同的分片服务器上，突破单机的容量限制。分片还有助于隔离，把毒丸请求的“爆炸半径”限制在所有服务器的一个子集内。搭建分片系统，需要对分片键和键哈希函数都有细致的理解与设计。找到正确的数据分区方式，往往决定了一个系统是可扩展，还是在扩展时陷入瓶颈。理解分片的细节，对于构建更大、更复杂的分布式系统至关重要。
